title: Create five-minute onboarding and sample repository

preExistingFromPriorCommit.message: MBR-1002: prepare onboarding and sample repository
preExistingFromPriorCommit.note: This task builds on that draft rather than replacing it: the offline fixture, its two fixture files, the sample repository README, and their test were already correct and were left as-is. This task's own work is docs/getting-started.md (rewritten for accuracy) and one new anti-drift test file.

notes: docs/getting-started.md documents six live-path steps (install prerequisites, enroll repository, activate client, request first packet, read receipt, force degradation) plus the pre-existing deterministic offline fixture as a zero-prerequisite alternative -- matching the task description's 'Guide install, enroll, client activation, first packet, receipt explanation, and forced-degradation demonstration.'

Every command in the live path was checked against real source before being written, per this task's hard rule against fabricated steps. Two inaccuracies in the prior draft were found and fixed: (1) step 6 referenced a `MEMBRANE_FEDERATE_URL` env var that does not exist anywhere in the codebase (verified by grep across mcp/*.mjs and docs/*.md) -- replaced with the real `CRYPT_PORT` env var mcp/client.mjs actually reads, with its real valid range (1024-65535) noted, since a value outside that range is silently ignored rather than erroring; (2) step 6 claimed forced degradation produces `providerStatus: "degraded"`, but reading mcp/client.mjs's transport-failure branch (lines ~338-360) shows a dead/unreachable service produces `providerStatus: "unavailable"` with `degradationReason: "planner_unavailable"` -- the doc now states the value the code actually produces.

A previously undocumented hard prerequisite was found and disclosed: mcp/installation-binding.mjs's non-dry-run `init`/`install` paths resolve installation binding by walking up from the target root for `tools/lib/memory/runtime.json` (RUNTIME_FILE). That file lives in the parent Orthic Labs workspace, not inside a standalone clone of this repository (confirmed: `find` for that path inside the membrane checkout alone returns nothing; it exists one level up at the parent workspace root). README.md's own 'Repository posture' section already discloses that this checkout is an internal mirror whose runtime wiring depends on the parent workspace; docs/getting-started.md now states this explicitly as a live-path prerequisite and links to that section, instead of documenting a step that would fail closed with `installation binding unavailable` for anyone outside that workspace.

The doc's steps were verified against the real mcp/install.mjs CLI, not merely inspected: `node mcp/install.mjs init <root> --repository demo-repo --scope demo-scope --dry-run` was run against examples/quickstart/repository and returned the documented {repository_id, scope_id, root} shape; a non-dry-run `init` (registry pointed at a scratchpad file, outside the repo) succeeded in this nested checkout, confirming the parent-workspace prerequisite note is accurate rather than speculative -- `git status --porcelain examples/` after that run showed no repository files changed. `install --client codex --dry-run` reached the real `codex mcp get membrane` subprocess call and surfaced a genuine local config conflict as a typed error, confirming the native-client integration path is real code, not aspirational. None of these verification runs are part of this task's required `node --test` evidence (see commands.log); they are additional due diligence the hard rules required before writing each step.

MBR-808's support-tier matrix dependency is honored two ways: (1) docs/getting-started.md's live-path prerequisites explicitly separate 'a native client's own CLI used against this source checkout' from the packaged installer's platform/client support tier, links docs/support-matrix.md, and states the current qualified count (0 of 10) rather than implying any platform/client combination is supported; (2) the new test's last case reads docs/support-matrix.json at test time and asserts the doc's literal 'N of M ... qualified' claim still matches the generated matrix, and additionally asserts the doc never claims more qualified pairs than the matrix backs -- so if MBR-801/MBR-808 later qualify a real pair and the doc is not updated, this test fails instead of the doc silently drifting into overclaiming.

membrane_context's exact required-field contract (task/repository/caller; caller.root/repositoryId/scopeId) was extracted from mcp/server.mjs's live TOOL_DEFINITIONS/CALLER_SCHEMA (not assumed) and the doc's example JSON payload matches it field-for-field; the new test asserts this via regex against mcp/server.mjs's real source so a future schema change that isn't mirrored in the doc fails the test.

tests/onboarding/getting-started-consistency.test.mjs is pure fs-read + regex/JSON comparison against real source files (mcp/install.mjs, mcp/client.mjs, mcp/server.mjs, mcp/project-registry.mjs, mcp/installation-binding.mjs, package.json, README.md, docs/support-matrix.json) -- no cargo/pnpm build, no network, no service, no import of mcp/server.mjs as a module (which would pull in node:sqlite and instantiate a ScratchpadStore at import time; avoided per Minimize -- textual verification is the smaller-footprint rung that still catches drift in the exact strings the doc depends on). It mechanically satisfies the hard rule that the five-minute claim's documented steps be checked for repo consistency so the doc cannot silently drift.

Acceptance ('A new user reaches proven non-zero delivery without reading architecture docs') is demonstrated two ways: mechanically, by the new test proving every live-path command/env-var/schema-field/support-tier-claim in the doc currently matches real source; and functionally, by the pre-existing offline fixture (tests/onboarding/quickstart.test.mjs, unchanged, still green) proving a deterministic, zero-prerequisite run of the exact commands in the doc's final section produces a receipt-bound packet in well under five minutes, honestly labeled `executionMode: fixture` / `evidenceAuthority: synthetic` so it is never mistaken for live delivery. Real live-path acceptance (an actual running Crypt loopback service, a real native client enrolling this checkout, and a real membrane_context round trip) was not run as part of this task -- per this task's hard rules against cargo/pnpm builds and per book-mode rules reserving qualification-grade runs for the final phased gate.

Modified only docs/getting-started.md and added tests/onboarding/getting-started-consistency.test.mjs, both inside this task's allowlist. Did not touch examples/quickstart/**, tests/onboarding/quickstart.test.mjs, apps/membrane-hub/** (reserved by a concurrent lane per the dispatching instructions, despite being in the manifest's allowedPaths), README.md, or docs/support-matrix.* -- those were read only. Left several concurrently-modified files from other lanes (docs/clients/support-matrix.v1.json, docs/release/macos.md, packages/python/**, evidence/productization/MBR-901/**, evidence/productization/MBR-909/**) untouched, per the primary-checkout multi-lane rule.

Set acceptanceStatus/acceptance.json status to pending_book_gate, not pass, and did not execute the manifest's `commands` list (cargo fmt --check, cargo test --workspace) -- both per book-mode execution rules reserving that for the final phased book gate.
